record.original_question: Given an ordinary differential equation whose solutions have the Painlevé property, determine whether the equation can be expressed in terms of one of the Painlevé transcendents or an associated Painlevé sigma-equation, and if so identify the correct Painlevé equation together with the transformation needed to convert the given equation into that standard form.

evidence.quote: Develop algorithmic procedures for the Painlev´e equivalence problem: given an equation with the Painlev´e property, how do we know if the equation can be solved in terms of a Painlev´e equation (or a Painlev´e σ-equation)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An ordinary differential equation is said to have the Painlevé property if every movable singularity of every solution (i.e., a singularity whose location depends on the initial conditions) is a pole. The six Painlevé equations P_I, P_II, ..., P_VI are the canonical second-order nonlinear ODEs (over the complex domain) whose general solutions have the Painlevé property and cannot, in general, be expressed in terms of classical special functions; their solutions are called Painlevé transcendents. To each Painlevé equation P_J there is an associated sigma-equation (Okamoto's auxiliary Hamiltonian form), a second-order ODE whose solutions are the Hamiltonians σ(t) along solutions of P_J.

Develop an algorithmic procedure for the following Painlevé equivalence problem. Given as input an ordinary differential equation
   F(t, y, y', y'', ..., y^{(n)}) = 0
which is known to possess the Painlevé property, decide:
 (1) whether its general solution can be expressed in terms of one of the six Painlevé transcendents (or, equivalently, in terms of an associated Painlevé sigma-equation);
 (2) if so, determine which Painlevé equation P_J (J ∈ {I, II, III, IV, V, VI}) — or which sigma-equation — it corresponds to; and
 (3) construct an explicit transformation (e.g. a change of dependent and independent variables, possibly together with auxiliary algebraic operations) that converts the given equation into the chosen standard Painlevé form.

Produce such an algorithm, or prove that no algorithm with these specifications exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The Painlevé equivalence problem is widely recognized as open in general. Recent work (2025) proposes step-by-step algorithmic procedures using the algebro-geometric theory of Okamoto's spaces of initial conditions and applies them to particular families (e.g., Bureau-Guillot systems), but a general algorithmic solution covering all ODEs with the Painlevé property has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic procedure for the Painlevé equivalence problem (arXiv 2508.12052)
status_evidence.snippet: A recent paper proposed an essentially algorithmic step-by-step procedure for solving the Painlevé equivalence problem using the algebro-geometric theory of Painlevé equations.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic procedures are still being actively developed; the problem is treated as open in general.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Bureau-Guillot systems ... birational equivalence (arXiv 2506.22896)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work has applied the geometric approach of Okamoto's spaces of initial conditions ... to solve the Painlevé equivalence problem for Bureau-Guillot systems with non-rational meromorphic coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for special classes of equations, but no general algorithm is established.
